findings.problem: The title guarantees elimination of all stale reads, contradicting the supplied snapshot contract and the narrative's own boundary and recap. Successful post-write deletion removes an entry already filled during the write, but the unchanged reader can cache an older snapshot after deletion. The modeled late-snapshot case reports a successful new stored value alongside an old cached value and an old subsequent read. The fill-during-write case also returns the old value to the overlapping reader even though deletion clears the cache. These modeled observations refute the title's universal guarantee under the supplied assumptions; they are not production measurements.

evidence.quote: db.read captures a snapshot when invoked, but its promise may fulfill after a later write commits.
Explicit promise gates schedule snapshot capture, write commit, and cache fill. One process and one Map; no wall-clock timing.

edits.value: Post-write invalidation closes one stale-fill window
